source_material: Owner supplied printed p.200 exact species treatment. Figure caption under E. megastachya is retained as historical synonym context; scan/figure not republished.

option.label: Gland pits along the blade midrib
option.detail: Inspect the midrib for glandular pits. A gland on a midrib does not establish a pale, raised or rough midvein.

option.label: Gland pits on the LOWER blade surface
option.detail: Turn the blade over. Gould describes gland pits on the midrib or lower surface; do not transfer sheath or glume glands to the blade.

option.label: Long hairs at the sheath throat
option.detail: Inspect the upper opening of the sheath. Gould describes an otherwise hairless sheath with a pilose throat. These throat hairs do not by themselves identify the actual inner ligule.

option.label: Gland pits on the sheath keel
option.detail: Trace the gland pits to the raised keel of the sheath, not a blade midrib, culm gland ring or lemma keel. Gould says usually, not always.

option.label: Gland pits on upper sheath nerves
option.detail: Inspect nerves near the top of the sheath. Gould says glands sometimes occur there; absence at this position does not exclude the species.

option.label: Spikelets carried on pedicels
option.detail: Check attachment of one spikelet to the panicle. A pedicellate spikelet is not automatically a bluestem-style paired sessile/stalked unit.

option.label: Gland pits on the OUTER glume keels
option.detail: Locate the two OUTER glumes before examining their keels. These glands are not lemma-keel glands, nor proof of any one-vein count.

option.label: Gland pits on the INNER lemma keel
option.detail: Open the glumes and locate the inner lemma. Gould says usually glandular-pitted on its keel; Diggs independently describes minute raised glandular dots on this keel.

option.label: Lemma membranous and dull
option.detail: Inspect the INNER lemma, not an outer glume. Gould describes closely overlapping membranous, dull gray-green lemmas; no shiny hard lemma is inferred.

evidence.note: Blades 2.5–7 mm wide and 10–20 cm long; both approximate narrow/medium bands apply.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Locate each gland on its actual organ
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould describes a gland ring below culm nodes; usually gland pits on the sheath keel, sometimes upper sheath nerves; blade midrib or lower-surface pits; glume-keel pits; and usually lemma-keel pits. Diggs corroborates minute raised glandular dots on the lemma keel.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: A gland on a culm, sheath or lemma cannot certify the gland state of KR’s sessile first glume. Glands may vary by position.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould p.200; Diggs named species p.1271; no local gland-bearing specimen certified.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Eragrostis cilianensis, printed p.200

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Count the many florets inside one spikelet
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould reports 12–40 florets within a 6–20 mm spikelet, 2–4 mm wide. The panicle is dense to open, with pedicellate spikelets. Persistent rachilla and paleas are separately described.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: These are many florets inside one spikelet, not KR’s sessile/stalked spikelet pair or finger count. Broader supplementary floret ranges remain documented.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould measurement; no new exclusion rule based on a usual or missing trait.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Eragrostis cilianensis, printed p.200

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate the hairy sheath throat from the true ligule
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould calls the sheath hairless except at its pilose throat, with overlapping sheaths and hairless flat or folded blades. This page does not describe the true ligule. The existing tiny hair-fringe ligule comes from separate regional evidence.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not turn long throat hairs into KR’s membranous ligule or blade-base papilla hairs. Tufted annual growth and odor alone do not certify identification.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould silence on ligule is not absence or a new ligule type; prior H&L evidence preserved.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Eragrostis cilianensis, printed p.200

secondary_reference_review.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, exact Eragrostis cilianensis account
secondary_reference_review.access: Directly read owner-connected reference PDF text; page footer 1271 verified after named treatment.
secondary_reference_review.corroborates: Annual, often strong odor; lemmas 2.2–2.8 mm with minute raised glandular dots on keel; disturbed sites; mostly August–October.
secondary_reference_review.limits: Exact named account does not specify every gland position or a ligule measurement. Do not misattribute genus-wide statements or supplementary ranges as named-species measurements.

non_scoring_context.panicle_shape: ovate to oblong, densely flowered to open

omissions_not_absences: Gould p.200 does not describe the ligule.
No new rhizome/stolon state inferred from basal branches or annuality.
No new vein counts inferred from conspicuous nerves without a number.
No papilla-based hairs inferred from gland pits.
Not every gland position must be expressed on every specimen.
